newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money traded 8.5/9.0 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money traded 8.5/9.0 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money was traded at 8.5/9.0 percent on Monday morning, dealers said.
They said liquidity was sufficient on central bank injection of some 389 billion rupiah into the market.
A local bank dealer said expectations of excess rupiah supply on Tuesday seemed to keep pressure on interbank rates on Monday following declines of swap premiums for all durations.
Overnight swap was at par/0.15 and tom/next at -0.1/0.1.
Dealers said one-week money was offered at 10.5 percent but no bid was seen in early trading. Three-month money fell to 13.25/13.75 percent from some 14.25 percent last week.
They said anticipation of ample liquidity resulted from heavy central bank dollar-buying last Friday to keep the dollar within the central bank intervention band.

The central bank offered two-day bilateral papers (SBIs) at seven percent, seven-day at 10.0 percent, 14-day at 10.75 percent, one-month at 12.0 percent, three at 12.75 percent, six at 13.00 and 12 at 13.25 percent.
The average overnight interbank rate on Friday was 11.9 percent, compared with 12.63 percent on Thursday.
